newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Friday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.

Traders said lending was intensified today after the China news service quoted Dai Xianglong, governor of People's Bank of China as saying that the central bank was considering cutting bank reserve ratios by 3.00 percentage points.

Dai did not gave a timetable, but the bank said in July that it would cut the ratio before the end of this year. Beijing now requires banks to save 13 percent of their deposits for the central bank and five to seven percent for themselves.
Traders said such a heavy cut in the ratio would mean large amounts of money would be released which would have a very big negative impact on the renminbi interbank market.
"Many banks increased their lending today on expectations of falls in market rates in the short term," one trader said.
The bulk of borrowing today came from securities houses and brokerages which raised money on the market to speculate in the surging domestic A shares, traders said.
Traders said the rates were likely to consolidate down in the short term before a real cut on the bank reserve ratios came into effect.
